claim: CAS does not dedup independently recomputed bytes (parts are not bit-reproducible across independent rebuilds due to compression block boundaries, codec defaults, and TTL now()); cross-replica dedup works only because one replica produces a part and others reference it.

Free carry-forward on mutation (re-referencing unchanged column blobs without recompute) applies only to Wide parts, whose default remote-disk threshold is 1 GiB; Compact parts are a single blob and are always fully rewritten on mutation.

A blob's identity H is a streaming, chunked cityHash128 computed incrementally via HashingWriteBuffer with block size DBMS_DEFAULT_HASHING_BLOCK_SIZE = 2048 as bytes are written, not a one-shot hash of a pre-existing buffer and not read from checksums.txt; the storage key is blobs/<H[:2]>/<H>.

A RefShard's journal is an append-only log of +/- ownership events retained until GC trim (gated by gc_trim_min_events / gc_trim_body_soft_limit settings) advances past the sealed fold cursor covering them (INV-JOURNAL-COVERAGE); the incarnation field is a durable strictly monotone (writer_epoch, build_sequence) pair stamped at (re)creation and never changed, closing the ABA hazard for a fold cursor keyed by (ns, shard, incarnation).

A PartManifest records (file_name -> blob_hash, size, placement) for every content-addressed file; EntryPlacement has Inline (tiny files embedded in the manifest body, part-open cost = 1 GET) and Blob (large standalone file at blobs/<H>); a third placement kind, pack_slice (member of a pack object at (pack_hash, abs_offset, length)), is a reserved design idea with no EntryPlacement enum value in the code.

Per-part write-time files uuid.txt, txn_version.txt, and metadata_version.txt are ordinary PartManifest entries, not a separate mutable sidecar; a single-file change on an already-committed part resolves through a committed-ref repoint that carries every unchanged entry forward and republishes one manifest, and a byte-identical rewrite is a zero-pool-mutation no-op (repointRef).

PartManifest bodies live at cas/manifests/<ns>/<writer_epoch>/<build_sequence>/<ordinal>.proto with a 6-digit zero-padded ordinal filename; a manifest's identity (ManifestId) is a root_namespace paired with a nested ManifestRef of (writer_epoch, build_sequence, manifest_ordinal), not a type literally named PartManifestId, and is unique by construction since every component is durable-monotone and never reused.

Nested sub-manifests per projection (each projection its own sub-PartManifest plus a projections footer) were rejected as a format/version change requiring a recursive resolver for identity projections never use, since projections are always read as children and rebuilt on merge (YAGNI). A separate projections/ ref namespace lifecycle-linked to the parent was also rejected as a second namespace plus GC coupling for no benefit.

The durable per-server_root_id identity is built from three sticky objects under gc/server-roots/<server_root_id>/: owner (permanent, putIfAbsent once, binds server_root_id to one server_uuid_hex forever), epoch (permanent, CAS-bumped per writable open, a durable monotone writer_epoch counter never reissued), and mount (an expirable heartbeat lease, same-UUID reclaim only after expiry).

server_root_id is a required, validated, immutable config parameter, not derived from ServerUUID; a superseded writer (whose writer_epoch no longer matches the live mount) issues no mutable CAS/PUT because the write-path lease fence is a local in-memory check with no per-write S3 read, tripping the disk to lost/fail-closed on any supersession.

The standalone watermark object and the gc/checkpoint/<n> full-GC checkpoint path shown in earlier design revisions do not exist in the current code: the build-watermark floor (min_active) was merged into the mount object as part of the ack-floor GC redesign, and gc/checkpoint/<n> has no corresponding key-builder in CasLayout.h.

A build heartbeat is durable in the pool before the first blob PUT via the pool-wide gc/hb pulse plus the writer's mount object build-watermark floor; there is no separate builds/<build_id> object in the current layout.

Upload by placement: new content is written PUT If-None-Match:* (idempotent, dedup hit skips upload); cold reuse of an existing blob point-reads the object's per-hash .meta freshness state (Core/CasBlobMeta.h, MetaState{Clean,Condemned}) — condemned triggers resurrect with a fresh incarnation_tag, else the blob is reused as-is; this point-read replaced the old writer-side retire view.

The build writes a precommit binding to a /_precommits namespace shard before publish, giving GC visibility into in-flight blobs; the fold barrier holds the +1 edge until the manifest body is present. Publish is one CAS PUT to the ref shard updating refs[part_name] and appending {+, name, T} to the journal atomically; tokened deps are edge-protected (EDGE-BEFORE-OBSERVE) and not re-checked at promote, while non-tokened deps get a per-hash .meta point-read and copy-forward-if-condemned inline in the blob-revalidation loop.

The current GC implementation (Gc class, CasGc.h) is a leader-paced ack-floor redesign (spec 2026-07-02): one pass per round consisting of a heartbeat ack floor over MountLease.observed_gc_round, a three-cursor merge fold, two-phase condemn/graduation deletion, and a single gc/state CAS; the older fence_round/recheck terminology survives only as fossil comments/variable names.
Regular GC deletion outcomes are classified as deleted | absent | replaced (412 = resurrection won) | spared, and retire entries are dropped only on confirmed outcomes.

A SQL DROP PART/DROP PARTITION is modeled as removal supersession: an additive commit creates a real part ref, a removal creates an empty covering tombstone ref promoted from MergeTreeData::dropPartImpl's local Outdated empty covering part into a persisted, Active, covering ref using the existing ActiveDataPartSet/getActiveContainingPart covering machinery. This persisted part ref is distinct from the D1 shard-object tombstone, which is a journal marker letting GC reclaim an empty shard object.

DROP PART has a documented weak guarantee under a mid-range race with a concurrent merge: the merge may produce a real covering part carrying the data, so DROP PART can end up merged into a bigger part instead of deleting it (ReplicatedMergeTreeLogEntryData::getVirtualPartNames returns {} for DROP_PART). The persisted tombstone for a mid-range single part is therefore conditional/reconciled, not unconditional: if a real covering part wins the race, the tombstone must not strand or double-cover.

FREEZE must materialize real bytes into the local shadow/ directory and cannot be reference-only, because shadow/'s documented contract is filesystem-readable hardlinks consumed by external backup pipelines; freeze/freezeRemote/clonePart are independent IDataPartStorage virtuals not built on createHardLinkFrom. A self-describing snapshots/<name> ref-set may exist as an additional in-pool reachability root for restore-by-reference but does not replace byte materialization.

Single-producer non-divergence enforced via a /merge_claims lease plus manifest_hash re-keying (v2 design) was replaced in v3 by tolerant-mode cross-replica commit checking: checkPartChecksumsAndCommit -> checkEqual(..., check_uncompressed_hash_in_compressed_files=true) compares uncompressed hashes, so two replicas with identical uncompressed content but different compressed bytes both pass, yielding at worst two manifests plus two blob sets for one part name (a benign dedup-miss, not a correctness bug; both sets are GC'd when the part is superseded).

A manifest_hash-on-znode idea (B1) to detect cross-replica manifest divergence was rejected outright (2026-07-14) on layering grounds: replication code stays disk-agnostic, and CA adds no field to the Keeper part header, because a CA-specific field in ReplicatedMergeTreePartHeader would couple ReplicatedMergeTree to one disk implementation, grow the fork's upstream-contact surface, and add states to already-complex replication. Fetch-by-relink needs no Keeper field either since the manifest id travels in-band over the interserver handshake.

The one writer-side path that fails closed on corruption is a detected logical-hash collision: in store_blob_safely, when a writer reuses an existing logical-hash key it verifies the existing object's header hashes to the expected logical hash (verify(existing_hdr.logical_hash == H)); if it does not, the system quarantines the key and raises a hard error rather than silently papering over the mismatch, since silent reuse of a mis-verifying object would let corrupt or colliding content be served under a live ref.

A Merkle treeId tree layer (content-addressed trees/<T> objects forming a Merkle DAG of immutable folders, with tree hashes carrying child_gen inside the tree identity) was rejected: child_gen inside tree identity forced ancestor rebuilds whenever a blob's generation floor moved, the 404->LIST degraded read path for generation resolution added latency and complexity, and the generation-in-key model required durable per-hash floors, epochs, per-build pins, quiescence machinery, and Keeper as a required component. It was replaced by the incarnation-token design; the trees/ key prefix and ObjectKind::Tree were removed entirely (2026-07-03) -- ObjectKind now has only Blob.

An EBR (Epoch-Based Reclamation) GC core -- writers holding a pin epoch (an ephemeral Keeper node), GC advancing through safe_epoch/commit_epoch/birth_epoch and waiting for quiescence, with generations on blob keys (blobs/<H>/<g>) as the ABA guard -- was rejected because a stuck or wedged writer held down safe_epoch and stalled reclamation of all dropped parts across all writers, Keeper was required for correctness, and a long-running INSERT could delay GC for its entire duration. It was replaced by the incarnation-token design, where regular GC candidates are restricted to journal-known nodes so fresh uploads are structurally invisible and can never be candidates, and a wedged writer has no pin to hold down.

Key invariants: INV-OVER-COUNT-ONLY -- every failure (lost fold, crashed leader, stale snap, duplicated records) delays reclamation but none accelerates a delete past the gates. INV-S3-COMPLETE -- S3 alone is both the durable truth and sufficient coordination; Keeper is an accelerator and total Keeper loss loses nothing and blocks nothing. INC-MONO -- for a fixed (ns, shard), every successive materialization of the shard object carries a strictly greater incarnation, closing ABA by construction. WriterEpochMonotoneUnique -- the epoch-object allocator never reissues a writer_epoch for a server_root_id, across crash/restart and across mount deletion.

The core invariants (INV-NO-LOSS, INV-NO-DANGLE, INV-NO-RETURN, INV-JOURNAL-COVERAGE, MonotoneGC) are model-checked by CaIncarnationCore.tla; mount-safety invariants (WriterEpochMonotoneUnique, SupersededWriterMakesNoMutation) are model-checked by a focused Phase-0 TLA+ model; INV-NO-DANGLING and INV-NO-ORPHAN-EDGE under D1 are model-checked by CaGcShardIncarnationCore.tla (724,944 states, GREEN as of 2026-07-01).

Backend safety depends on exact-token conditional delete: a DELETE If-Match token with a wrong token MUST fail, not silently succeed; this is probed at startup and the disk fails closed if the backend does not enforce it. Bucket versioning must never be enabled on the CA prefix; versioning-suspended buckets are also rejected because a delete inserts a null delete marker, breaking the one-live-object model. A startup probe verifies this functionally.

Backend conformance table: AWS S3 (versioning off) uses ETag, fully conforming, validated live 2026-07-03, probe-gated at startup (DeleteObject If-Match GA'd Sep 2025). RustFS 1.0.0-beta.8 uses ETag, empirically verified 2026-06-11, leading open-source CI candidate, with known issue rustfs#3231 (overwrite-leak of objects above the store's inline threshold, e.g. 128 KiB, in unversioned buckets) that can produce metacache LIST storms and false 404s on HEAD -- the only source of GC fold clamps observed to date. Azure Blob uses ETag (write-sensitive), supported and probe-gated, with versioning/soft-delete required off. GCS uses generation, binding specified but implementation deferred, fail-closed until probed. MinIO OSS (archived 2026-02) has If-Match on DELETE silently ignored (confirmed 2026-06-11) -- fail-closed. Ceph RGW has no conditional delete documented -- fail-closed.

As of the architecture doc: probe logic for backend conditional-delete conformance is DONE; GCS generation binding is TODO; versioned mode (token = versionId) is a future, explicitly separate feature.

Store::~Store() can abort() the process: a lease-renewal failure during teardown re-arms remount_thread after the destructor's only join, because scheduleRemount() gates only on config.background_watermark and remount_running (never on a shutdown flag), so a fresh ThreadFromGlobalPool gets move-assigned into remount_thread after the join already passed; both ThreadFromGlobalPoolImpl::operator=(&&) and its destructor call abort() on a still-initialized target, so member destruction aborts. This is a guaranteed process crash under a realistic interleaving (an ordinary fenced-out or transiently-failing mount lease during DROP/disk-detach/server-shutdown), and was rated a blocker (risk 90) in the umbrella review of cas-gc-rebuild.

Proposed fix for the Store::~Store() teardown abort: add a remount_shutting_down flag set under remount_thread_mutex at the very top of ~Store(); make scheduleRemount() check it first and refuse to spawn once set; re-join remount_thread after mount_keeper->stop(); and give MountLeaseKeeper its own destructor (stopBackground()) so the renewal thread is always joined before its std::function members are destroyed.

An umbrella review of the cas-gc-rebuild branch flagged a table-level RBAC/confidentiality-bypass finding in the fetch-by-relink path (a peer could bind any live pool blob into a low-privilege table via wire-supplied manifest entries). This finding was later retracted as not-a-bug: the interserver channel is the same trust boundary an ordinary ReplicatedMergeTree part fetch already has, and this is documented in code rather than fixed as a vulnerability.

The CAS read path re-parses the full part path on every IMetadataStorage call (existsFile/getFileSize/getStorageObjects/... each independently run parsePartFilePath plus route with ~10-15 small allocations), versus 1-2 allocations for non-CAS metadata backends; getView's cache-hit path additionally takes the per-table state_mutex and per-disk explain_mutex (a test/log-only decision journal) on every file-open plus two cacheKey() heap allocations, causing real serialization on wide-table/high-concurrency CAS SELECTs. Proposed fix: resolve the route once per file-open (memoize per raw path) and make the explain journal opt-in behind a setting, disabled by default.

PocoHTTPClient injects Expect: 100-continue by default for any conditional S3 PUT >= 1 MiB (S3Defines.h DEFAULT_EXPECT_CONTINUE_MIN_BYTES = 1 MiB), applying to all S3 traffic including the pre-existing non-CAS Iceberg conditional-commit path, with no CAS-specific gate; this exists because of a real ~40-minute production stall (B118) but has zero test coverage. Proposed fix: scope it to CAS-owned writes via a WriteSettings flag (as done for s3_force_single_part_upload), or document the expect_continue_min_bytes default in release notes, plus add a mock-HTTP-server test for the 100-continue / body-skip branches.

dropRefBestEffort swallows rollback failure with no logging: a correlated backend outage during partial-commit rollback can leave a permanently-live phantom ref, since GC only reclaims unreferenced objects and won't clean it up. Proposed fix: add tryLogCurrentException (CachedPartFolderAccess.cpp).

MultipleDisksObjectStorageTransaction has a latent bad_weak_ptr risk: a double enable_shared_from_this base means the CA writeFile pinning subclass is not reachable today only because cross-disk CA copy hits a different path first (DiskObjectStorageTransaction.h). Proposed fix: drop the redundant base.

The two new CAS system logs (content_addressed_log, content_addressed_garbage_collection_log) ship enabled-by-default, yet SystemLog.h documents content_addressed_log as "off by default" -- the comment and config.xml default disagree and need reconciling.

Umbrella review open items needing verification: whether mixed CA + non-CA (tiered hot/cold) storage policies are a supported/tested topology (governs severity of a relink pool-UUID mis-advertise bug); whether an unreachable CAS bucket at boot actually aborts whole-server DiskSelector::initialize() (traced in code, not run); Expect:100-continue behavior against real AWS S3, MinIO, Ceph RGW, and transparent HTTP proxies (only RustFS/GCS validated); blast radius of two concurrent GC rounds sharing one gc_id.

CasEvent::round was NOT removed despite the original stabilization spec calling it a dead always-0 field with 5 write sites; at HEAD it has 20 write sites, is copied into ContentAddressedLogElement::round, and is a live serialized system.content_addressed_log.round column, so deleting it would be a user-visible schema change.

The single-value ObjectKind enum was NOT removed (spec item D1f) despite being a single-valued enum: it is threaded as the parameter/field type of observeAndAdmit, uploadFromSource, decodeEnvelopeHeader, magicFor, retiredLogicalSize, EnvelopeHeader::kind, RetiredEntry::kind, the CasGcOutcomes codec, and Fsck/GcObserved, with ~100 consumers; removing it is a refactor, not a subtraction.

Task A5's detached-part-path fix anchors the reserved `detached` directory component left-to-right (first match), not the right-to-left scan the original spec sketched, because a right-to-left scan would incorrectly anchor on the inner part-dir-shaped component first.

Task A6's skip_access_check fix covers only the Ring-0 CAS Store::open probe gate; generic per-disk isolation of the flag through IDisk::startup(bool)/DiskSelector (global_skip_access_check) remains deferred to a separate 'Group G' upstream-plumbing effort.

Task A7 serializes the manual `SYSTEM ... GC` round against the background GC loop using a dedicated gc_round_mutex rather than the scheduler's existing `mutex`, because loop() deliberately releases `mutex` before running a round so that stop() and heartbeatLoop() are not blocked; holding `mutex` across a long fold would freeze the GC heartbeat and stall shutdown.

A one-line-per-site revert of copyS3File's message_format_string usage back to PreformattedMessage::create(...) (copyS3File.cpp:68-74,126-138, spec §7 Group G) was identified but not authored as a standalone task in the stabilization plan; it is intended to fold into the R412 commit or land as a trivial follow-up, and is called out explicitly so it is not lost.

Cross-task coordination for the stabilization plan: within Phase 3, sub-item D1d (removing ShardCoverage::folded_cursor/incarnation) must run before D5 (the gtest_cas_dangling_precommit.cpp rename) since both touch the same `cov.folded_cursor = 7;` test line; Phase-2 task A7 must land before Phase-5 task B3 since B3's gcHealth() reads gc_scheduler under A7's gc_scheduler_mutex.

Deferred refactors explicitly out of scope for the stabilization plan (spec §6): a CasGc.cpp split, de-god-classing Cas::Store, DiskSelector per-disk isolation, DiskObjectStorageTransaction part-path virtualization, removeFileIfExists+writeFile ordering dead code, and a latent MultipleDisks shared_from_this issue.

Parallel, non-blocking 'track G' items intended to be upstreamed separately to shrink the fork's diff long-term: the ThreadStatus fix (B90), ReadBufferFromFileView fix (B115), ReadBufferFromS3 fix (B117), a LocalObjectStorage TOCTOU fix, a MergeTreeDeduplicationLog null-writer fix, the copyS3File message-format revert, a generic opt-in Expect:100-continue negotiation, S3Exception::isPreconditionFailed, and GCS dialect/signer support.

The residual Late-Predecessor-PUT ref-loss race is mitigated only by the snapshot_min_log_age_ms grace window (a candidate ref snapshot never covers a tail region younger than this age); ProfileEvents::CasRefLatePredecessorObserved increments once per trySnapshotPublishOnce call in which that grace window forces an early break, making the residual race measurable rather than only mitigated.

system.content_addressed_mounts types server_uuid as UUID and started_at_ms/expires_at_ms as DateTime64(3) (previously String and raw UInt64 unix-ms); the ContentAddressedLog system-log description was corrected from 'optional, off by default' to reflect that it is enabled by default while the CA disk feature is experimental.

The dangling-precommit TLA+ gate adds constant `SabotageSkipParksDeadPrecommit` and liveness property `LiveDeadPrecommitReclaimed` to `CaGcRootLocalPartManifestCore.tla`; the bug config must violate the property (a watermark-dead live precommit's manifest body stutters present forever under Skip) and the fix config must hold it.

The force-Read override HEADs only fire from `closeBlob` on hashes touched in the current fold window (`cur_edges == 0`); `settleRetiredBelow`'s quiescent-entry path never issues a HEAD and must not be changed to do so.
On a resurrect supersede the fold keeps exactly one retired entry per hash: the stale entry is dropped, not kept alongside the fresh re-condemn, and the retired list stays hash-sorted.

A BACKLOG item requires a GC per-table recovery gate (abort-only clamp) before the fold extracts manifest edges, because the fold currently trusts codec-valid transactions without state-machine replay; this gate is mandatory before multi-writer or rolling-upgrade-skew milestones ship.

E5's in-place-materialize fast path was unreachable from production: `flushRefBatch`'s trial-validation copy `working` stayed alive to function scope, pinning a second shared_ptr reference to the live base across the post-PUT install so `materializeCommitted()` always saw `use_count()==2` and took the O(N) copy path; fixed by releasing `working` before id allocation so the live base is uniquely owned at the install point.

A race existed where the relaxed `use_count()` load in the in-place-materialize fast path could race a cross-thread shared_ptr release: `trySnapshotPublishOnce`'s `candidate_state` (a shared-base copy) was destroyed at function return outside the lock. Fixed by resetting `candidate_state` under `state_mutex` immediately after `snapshotOf`, covering every exit path.

Every cross-thread copy of a live `RefTableState` must be created AND destroyed under `state_mutex`, so that a `use_count()` of 1 observed under that lock is stable against both increment and decrement; this invariant is documented in both COW headers (`RefCowMap`, `RefCowManifestSet`).

The in-place fold's coherence ordering: per overlay entry, the base mutation (its only throw point) runs first, then the non-throwing `net_delta` adjust and `overlay.erase`; at every escape point `(base, overlay, net_delta)` stays exactly coherent, load-bearing because materialize runs after a durable PUT and a tracked-allocator OOM must not corrupt live bookkeeping.

In-place trusted-replay apply is safe because every production call site of `admits`/`applyRefLogTxn`/`replay` runs either under the ledger's `state_mutex` or on a detached/local copy, so no concurrent reader can observe a state mid-mutation; COW writes touch only the per-copy overlay, never the shared immutable base.

`admits` was deliberately left as a scratch-copy preview rather than converted to in-place apply, because its only production call site (`item_scratch`, a detached local) copies an O(batch) overlay, not an O(N) one, so making it in-place would add complexity for no measured win.

The recovery-latency fix (G) materializes only the one retained recovery-adopt site (`CasRefLedger.cpp:426`) before retaining its replayed state; the fsck/GC `replay`/`recoverRefTable` locals (`CasFsck.cpp`, `CasOrphanManifestSweep.cpp`, `CasGc.cpp`) are iterated once and dropped, so they are deliberately left unmaterialized.

The `LOGICAL_ERROR` ASan-abort triage found four coherent production-invariant groups with their guard sites: mount single-writer/lifecycle guards in `CasServerRoot.cpp:695-711,807-865,941-944`; part-write lifecycle and dependency-closure guards in `CasPartWriteTxn.cpp:125-129,329-337,520-524,818-823,895-900,986-992`; ordered/reserved-identifier guards in `CasBlobInDegree.cpp:176-181`, `CasRecordStreamFormat.cpp:156-168`, `CasTypes.h:242-249`; and a snapshot seal-bound guard in `CasRefSnapshotFormat.cpp:93-101`.

The recommended remediation order for the LOGICAL_ERROR ASan triage is: (1) swap the one Class A hook from `LOGICAL_ERROR` to `S3_ERROR`; (2) convert the 19 direct Class B negative assertions to `EXPECT_DEATH`, including the worker-thread heartbeat case; (3) repair the three incidental teardown fixtures so the primary test cleans up validly while the release guard gets an isolated death assertion; (4) remove the Class D test from the logical-error list pending a captured, reproducible failure.

For the three Class B tests whose `LOGICAL_ERROR` aborts fire incidentally at teardown rather than being the stated test subject (`CasGcRound.OrphanManifestCursorSweepDeletesAndPersistsCursor`, `CasMountStartup.StaleSelfMountReclaimedAfterWait`, `CasPoolRemount.ForeignOwnerIsNeverTakenOver`), the safest remediation is to keep the primary behavior test's cleanup valid and add or isolate an `EXPECT_DEATH` assertion for the release guard; if the existing test is retained as the release-guard test, the entire invalid setup plus explicit destruction must live inside the death statement.

To capture a jemalloc heap profile on a build where `SYSTEM JEMALLOC ENABLE PROFILE` is deprecated, set `<jemalloc_enable_global_profiler>1</jemalloc_enable_global_profiler>` in server config and restart, then read symbolized samples via `SELECT line FROM system.jemalloc_profile_text SETTINGS jemalloc_profile_text_output_format='symbolized'` (jeprof-compatible with embedded symbols, no binary needed).

On the studied Altinity build, `SYSTEM JEMALLOC FLUSH PROFILE` writes a `.heap` file plus an empty `.heap.collapsed` and no `.symbolized` file, and `system.asynchronous_metrics`'s `jemalloc.prof.active` can read 1 even when `prof.thread_active_init=0` and zero backtrace samples are actually captured, making the async metric misleading for confirming profiler state.

To make a CAS soak's tracked-memory gate reflect CAS behavior rather than the profiler firehose, either disable the harness's 10 ms query profiler for S23 or subtract the `DB::SystemLog` flush working set from the tracked-memory measurement.

Whole-object copy-on-write for `RefTableState::committed` via `src/Common/COW.h` (clone the whole map on any write) was rejected as "approach C" because trial copies during a flush always write, so it gives no gain over the naive full-map copy.

The `RefCowMap` COW-overlay design for `RefTableState::committed` reuses the same immutable-base-plus-delta pattern Keeper already uses for `KeeperStorage::UncommittedState` (`Delta`/`applyDelta`/`rollback` over a committed `Container`), specialized to an ordered map.
The `RefCowMap` design's correctness/testing plan requires the existing `Ca*:Cas*` gtest battery to stay green at 905/905 as evidence that behavior is byte-identical.

The `RefTableState` closed-class optimization design lists three residual risks: E3's overlay-level transaction layer moves the strong-exception-safety guarantee into new code and needs an explicit test that state is byte-for-byte unchanged after a throwing transaction; E4's flat-vector base has different iterator-invalidation rules than the old node-based map, so the closed class's read API must not leak the old iterator-stability promises; and `cas-gc-rebuild` is a shared branch worked concurrently by another session, requiring commit discipline (verify `HEAD` after commit, one ninja at a time, never rebase/amend).

In the `RefTableState` experiment matrix, E3 (transaction-layer instead of scratch copy) composes with E2 (COW owned-manifest index) or E4 (flat sorted-vector base) since a transaction layer works over either base, and E1 (relaxed replay) reduces the weight of what E2 must speed up; the comparison table is expected to judge combinations, not only single experiments.

Before an F1 propagation fix, a read-only `Store::open` still called `PoolMeta::createOrValidate` unconditionally (`CasStore.cpp:122,134`), which does `casPut(..., expected=nullopt)` (create-if-missing, `CasPoolMeta.cpp:129`); over an EMPTY/wrong prefix this either mutates storage or throws a write-permission error instead of cleanly reporting "pool absent" — only the capability probe was skipped for `read_only`, not the meta write. Only bites read-only-over-empty; over a live pool with existing `_pool_meta` the call only validates.

`ObjectStorageBackend::list` in `EmulatedSingleProcess` mode fills `lk.token` from `child->metadata->etag` (`CasObjectStorageBackend.cpp:781-783`) while emulated `head`/`get`/`putOverwrite`/`deleteExact` all use `emuObserveToken`; a consumer that reuses `listed.token` for `deleteExact` (the orphan-manifest sweep, `CasOrphanManifestSweep.cpp:300`) can get a token mismatch and leave GC debris undeleted in that test-only mode. Production `Native` S3 is unaffected because both `list` and `head` return the real S3 ETag.

fsck's manifest-debris pass discovers namespaces via `store.listNamespaces` (`CasFsck.cpp:371`), which enumerates only `cas/refs/` and `roots/` (`CasStore.cpp:1640`), not `cas/manifests/`; a namespace whose only remnant is a staged `cas/manifests/...` body that `Build::abandon`'s best-effort cleanup missed (`CasBuild.cpp:958`) is not enumerated, so fsck under-reports it as unreachable even though the GC orphan sweep (which scans `cas/manifests/` directly) still reclaims it — a fsck diagnostics gap, not a leak.

The new CAS S3 functional-test CI lane calls `CH.start_rustfs()`, which only checks for a pre-existing `ci/tmp/rustfs` binary and returns `False` if missing; unlike `setup_minio.sh` for MinIO, no tracked script downloads/extracts the RustFS binary, so the lane fails deterministically on a clean CI runner. Fix direction: add a tracked `setup_rustfs.sh` mirroring `setup_minio.sh` that pulls/extracts the `rustfs/rustfs:1.0.0-beta.8` static binary into `ci/tmp/rustfs`, invoked before the CAS s3 job's `start()`.

Sharded-GC correctness was validated by S15: identical oracle checksums and `dangling=0` under both `gc_shards=1` (default) and `gc_shards=2`, with reducer memory flat (0.60->0.61 GB) and orphan backlog fully drained in both configurations.

During the 4h chaos soak, the detail=False summary fsck exceeded its 180 s bound at ~183 GB / 2.14M objects at the gc_checkpoint, so the harness's `dangling==0` safety gate was skipped (`fsck_status: skipped`) rather than failing — the quadratic discovery/LIST cost blinds the correctness oracle at this pool size (tracked as B146/B154).

During the 4h chaos soak (SOAK-4H-DISK-INFEASIBLE), the `max_pool_gb=40` insert-pacing throttle could not hold the cap: the pool crossed 40 GB by ~t+30min and kept climbing (~5 GB/min decelerating to ~1.8 GB/min under full throttle) because RustFS performs no background compaction and MergeTree merge/mutation write-amplification plus non-reclaim outpace insert-pacing; growth stopped cleanly only when inserts stopped, at a ~183 GB plateau.

During the 4h chaos soak, the soak harness's own `pool_objects` telemetry returned `None` for the entire run and `pool_bytes` returned `None` on roughly half the ticks under write load; the throttle fails closed on `None` (treats it as `_THROTTLE_MAX`), and an independent `du`-based resource monitor gave ground truth instead — the soak's own pool telemetry is unreliable at scale.

A five-hour CA soak validation round found a genuine PRODUCT BUG in S22: `CasBlobMeta.cpp`'s `putMetaIfAbsent`/`casMeta`/`deleteMetaExact` hit the backend directly, the only hot-path conditional-write class outside `CasRequestController`, so an injected `SlowDown` fault gets one SDK attempt with zero controller-level retries and escapes to the client as an HTTP 500; the fix reroutes these through the controller and adds a new controlled If-Match variant plus a fault gtest.

An R5-round review found a CRITICAL trust-flip bug where finding #19's guard made `CasProbe` vacuous on Native S3 pools: wrong-dialect probe tokens were being rejected locally before ever going over the wire, at three call sites in `CasProbe.cpp:93,143,172`; the fix applies a live-dialect probe at all three sites plus a reachability test that pins non-vacuousness.

An ASan battery run found 7 genuine memory-safety bugs among 49 peeled aborts: 6 stack-use-after-scope instances in `CasSweepLateLog`-family tests, root-caused to an event-sink lambda capturing a local `events` vector declared AFTER the `Pool` object, so `~Pool` emits terminate events into the already-destroyed vector (fixed by declaring the vector before the Pool); and 1 heap-use-after-free in `CasPoolShutdown.UnresolvedWedgeSkipsFarewell`, root-caused to a `const Layout &` held across `store.reset()` (fixed by taking it by value).

The ASan battery's culprit-detection scripts used plain `grep` (not `grep -a`) on archived round logs containing thousands of embedded NUL bytes from CAS blob payloads in stdout, causing silent misattribution: rounds 27-66 (39 consecutive rounds) were all the same unfixed `CasRefSnapshotFormat.RejectsSnapshotIdBelowSealedFrom` abort, never actually excluded, so the peeling loop looped on one bug while accumulating ~30 wrong bystander test names in the known-debt list; the fix switched the scripts to `grep -a` and the exclusion list was corrected from 58 down to 28 verified real culprits.

A five-hour CA validation round found an unresolved architecture-level race in CAS pool decommission/owner-retirement: after a mount's owner is deleted and its epoch is already gone, a same-UUID successor can recreate the mount untouched by the owner check, and decommission's delete then removes the live successor's owner anchor; a symmetric owner-token check alone cannot close this because the owner's token never changes on resume, so a fix needs either a symmetric successor-side recheck or a condemn-marker two-phase retirement touching the claim/resume protocol, not just `CasDecommission.cpp`.

For sanitizer/debug-build-deterministic `EXPECT_DEATH` tests covering genuine `LOGICAL_ERROR` invariant violations, force `DB::abort_on_logical_error.store(true)` inside the death-test child process (an existing production knob, `Exception.h:34`) to get cross-build-type determinism and matchable abort message text.

`decommissionPoolMember` throws `CORRUPTED_DATA` when a catalog entry is `Removing` but its exact checkpoint (`refCkptKey`) is absent from the backend, refusing to retire the victim slot for that namespace.

`decommissionPoolMember`'s only list-based deletions target three physically loose non-catalog debris prefixes rooted at the victim's own server-root subtree — the manifest sweep, the staging drain (`<pool_prefix>/staging/<victim_srid>/`), and the mountpoint drain (`<pool_prefix>/roots/<victim_srid>/`) — and none of them participates in namespace-ownership selection.

`gtest_cas_holey_list_detector.cpp`'s two kept tests (`OmittedRemoveRecordIsSkippedForever`, `OmittedActivationNeverPermitsDeletingALiveBlob`) prove the arithmetic ref-intake's resilience to a holey LIST page independently of probe A, a class of coverage unrelated to and unaffected by probe A's removal.

`build/t5_inventory_before.txt` and `build/t5_inventory_after.txt` (429 lines) were force-committed inside the gitignored `build/` directory; recommended follow-up is `git rm --cached` since the inventory classification already lives in the task report.

The `FrontierUnproven::NoCatalogEntry` and `AppendAboveFrozenTail` buckets were removed outright (not retained with a comment) once they became unfireable-by-construction, because a zero-only bucket cannot change the invariant `sum(buckets) == frontier_namespaces - frontier_proven`, and retaining a dead enumerator would falsely imply a live exit path to a reader.

`WalkTarget::frozen_tail` was deleted as an unread field (written at three `push_back` sites, read nowhere) once the frozen-tail break arm it supported was removed as dead code, since keeping the field with prose claiming it bounds the round would have been a false statement about the code.

Under `suppress_destructive`, both the `manifest_deletes` phase and the orphan sweep are gated closed: `mf_cleanup_now` is an empty map, and the orphan-sweep delete loop consumes `folded.orphan_sweep.nominations`, which is empty because `planManifestCursorPage` is only invoked when `!suppress_destructive`.

Running a CAS stateless test directly via `tests/clickhouse-test` against a manually-started `clickhouse-server` binary (no configured praktika lane) requires exporting `CLICKHOUSE_USER_FILES` to match the server's actual data path; the harness's default `/var/lib/clickhouse/user_files` mismatch makes the pool directory invisible to the server, producing `Unknown disk` with `baseline=0 after_insert=0`.

The frontier round's "universe" is exactly every `Live`/`Removing` row of the round's own frozen catalog cut and nothing else; an older comment defining it as "hint ∪ sealed cursors ∪ catalog Live/Removing entries" is stale and contradicts the code, which implements only the catalog-cut definition.
